chapter_title: Chương 2: Sách hay giúp bạn trưởng thành

segments.title: Chương 2: Sách hay giúp bạn trưởng thành
segments.content:
Chen Guiliang's spot was at a transportation hub on campus, where there was also a row of promotional bulletin boards.

He found a large, leafy banyan tree, squatted down under it, and opened his worn-out suitcase.

The second-year students were on break for the past two days, vacating their classrooms for the third-years' exams. The first-years, however, were still having classes as usual, and occasionally, you could see students heading to and from P.E. class.

Chen Guiliang took out his books and magazines, arranged them neatly, and sat cross-legged, waiting for an opportunity to attract business.

When he was younger, he was thin-skinned and easily ashamed, not cut out for business.

He remembered the summer after junior high graduation, when he carried a load of bamboo shoots to the city. He had set out at 4:30 in the morning and stood foolishly at a wet market on the urban-rural fringe from morning until noon, without selling a single bamboo shoot!

In the afternoon, starving, he carried the untouched bamboo shoots all the way back home.

He never set up a stall again after that.

Thinking back on it now, it was pitiably foolish.

Reborn, Chen Guiliang silently observed the students coming and going.

You couldn't just shout out your sales pitch blindly; you had to read people and choose the right targets.

For example, the few boys who had just run past, chasing and roughhousing while dribbling a basketball. Their eyes were only on the basketball court, eager to claim a hoop. Even if you pinned them down in front of the bookstall, they wouldn't buy anything.

A full twenty minutes passed before four girls came by, eating ice cream bars and walking together.

They chattered and laughed nonstop. One of them cast a glance at the bookstall, and her pace noticeably slowed.

Chen Guiliang's eyes were sharp. He immediately called out, "Hey, student, want to buy some books? I've got famous works from all times and places. I'm a third-year about to sprint for the Gaokao, selling my books to focus. The prices are so cheap it's practically a giveaway."

These girls were first-years, having been at the school for just over two months.

To put it more bluntly: they were easy to fool!

Tao Xue's home was in the city. Her love for literature and admiration for Guo Xiaosi had brought her to study in this county town.

The school's atmosphere was indeed liberal, even to the point of being somewhat lax, turning a blind eye even to puppy love among students.

Her roommates went to buy ice cream even as the weather cooled in autumn. Passing the bulletin boards, Tao Xue saw someone selling books from a stall, and she subconsciously slowed her steps.

She hadn't planned on buying anything, but upon hearing the seller's words, Tao Xue approached out of curiosity.

She slurped her ice cream and asked, "Do you have *The Edge of Love and Pain*?"

In truth, she had read the book several times. Mentioning it now was merely a way to show off her taste.

Chen Guiliang grinned, his words flowing freely. "You're a fan of Guo Xiaosi? What a coincidence, I happen to know him. He was the president of our school's literature club in '01, and I was the president in '02. Get it? We're successive presidents."

"Really?" Tao Xue was skeptical.

Chen Guiliang said, "Would I lie to you? The current president of the literature club was nominated by me."

Tao Xue couldn't help but ask, "Senior, what's your name?"

Chen Guiliang said, "My name is Zhang Wei, from Class 1 of the third year. Are you in the literature club too?"

He just made that up on the spot, very much in the style of Dr. Ma. Tao Xue nodded and said, "Yeah, the literature club was recruiting a while back, so I filled out a form and became a member. Senior Zhang Wei, do you have Guo Xiaosi's phone number? His QQ number would be fine too."

"Guo Xiaosi is very busy, I can't just give out his personal information," Chen Guiliang quickly picked out a book. "I think this copy of *Dream of the Red Chamber* is perfect for a literary young lady with such depth as yourself."

Another girl with long hair glanced at it. "This is a pirated copy, isn't it?"

Chen Guiliang quickly flipped through the pages. "Look at this print quality, look at this binding and book jacket. Even if it's pirated, it's a high-quality pirated copy. Besides not having an ISBN, what's the difference from the original? I bought it last year for 20 yuan. It's still ninety percent new, I'll sell it to you for 5 yuan!"

Tao Xue took *Dream of the Red Chamber* and stood there flipping through it carefully, finding that it really was no different from the authentic version.

She had actually read *Dream of the Red Chamber* in junior high, but Chen Guiliang was so enthusiastic that she found it hard to refuse.

Suddenly, an idea struck her. Tao Xue asked, "Senior, which character is your favorite? I like Xue Baochai."

This was her roundabout way of reminding Chen Guiliang that she had read the book and didn't need to buy it again.

Chen Guiliang seemed not to understand and gave a startling reply, "I like Granny Liu the most."

"Huh?" Tao Xue was very surprised.

Her three roommates were also sent into fits of laughter.

Someone actually liked Granny Liu?

Chen Guiliang used the table of contents of *Dream of the Red Chamber* to quickly find the part where Granny Liu appeared. "Everyone uses 'Granny Liu entering the Grand View Garden' to describe someone unsophisticated making a fool of themselves. You all think Granny Liu is a comical character?"

The girls nodded instinctively.

"Granny Liu knows when to advance and when to retreat, she's very shrewd in how she handles things. Look here," Chen Guiliang said, flipping the pages, "when visiting someone's home, Ban'er whined for meat, and Granny Liu smacked him one. Do you think she's someone who doesn't know the rules?"

"And look here. Granny Liu has her pride too. It's obvious she's swallowing her pride for the sake of survival. Her conversation with Sister Feng, every sentence is a subtle confrontation, using retreat as a means of advance, putting Wang Xifeng in a position where she couldn't refuse."

"By observing Wang Xifeng's interaction with Jia Rong, Granny Liu completely figured out Wang Xifeng's personality. The four words here, 'her mind was finally at ease,' weren't written casually by Cao Xueqin. It shows that Granny Liu was already confident. The next line, 'your nephew,' directly put Wang Xifeng on the spot. If she didn't give her some money, she would lose face."

"After all the trouble of begging for twenty taels of silver, she took the initiative to leave one tael for Zhou Rui's wife. She's smart, eloquent, polite, not greedy, and knows to repay kindness. In her conduct, Granny Liu not only crushes Zhou Rui's wife, but even Wang Xifeng seems immature in front of her."

"The only thing Granny Liu lacks is worldliness."

Hearing Chen Guiliang's analysis, Tao Xue felt that Granny Liu was indeed on a very high level.

How come she hadn't seen that when she read *Dream of the Red Chamber*?

Chen Guiliang continued flipping through the book. "You all think Granny Liu is comical and embarrassing, but Wang Xifeng didn't think so. Look at Chapter 113 here. Wang Xifeng knew her life was coming to an end. In the entire vast Jia residence, she trusted no one. Yet, she thought of entrusting her daughter to Granny Liu. If you had a daughter and were gravely ill with not long to live, would you entrust your daughter to a foolish old country woman?"

Tao Xue began to think seriously.

Chen Guiliang said, "Because Wang Xifeng knew in her heart that Granny Liu repays kindness, values relationships and righteousness, and is both brave and resourceful, far more reliable than those people in the Jia residence. The most correct choice she ever made in her life was, before she died, to force her daughter to acknowledge Granny Liu as her godmother. When no one in the Jia family could protect her daughter, only Granny Liu would step forward to help out of a sense of justice."

Tao Xue had a sudden realization and said with admiration, "Senior, you're amazing. No wonder you could be the president of the literature club!"

Chen Guiliang smiled and stuffed *Dream of the Red Chamber* into her hands. "So, you should read this book over and over. Every time you read it, you'll gain new insights. Five yuan, take the book."

Tao Xue absentmindedly paid, only remembering after she bought it that she already had a copy at home.

But she felt too embarrassed to return it.

To prevent Tao Xue from changing her mind, Chen Guiliang had already started talking to the other three girls. "Would you like me to recommend a few books? This one, *The Silver Age*, is pretty good. It's by Wang Xiaobo, witty, humorous, and profound."

A chubby girl flipping through a magazine asked, "Are these really two jiao a copy?"

"Three for five jiao, eight for one yuan," Chen Guiliang enthusiastically promoted. "*Reader* and *Yilin* are both great magazines, especially the articles about foreign countries. They can broaden our horizons."

The scams he had fallen for in his past life, he naturally had to make others experience them after his rebirth. "You're only in your first year now. Reading more *Reader* and *Yilin* will not only increase your knowledge but also improve your writing skills. That Big Foot ice cream bar of yours costs five jiao, right? The ice cream is gone in a few bites, but for the same price, you can buy some of the world's best magazines. What a bargain!"

The girls thought his words made sense. Even Tao Xue, who had just bought *Dream of the Red Chamber*, gave up the idea of returning it and started picking out magazines instead.

They were cheap anyway, good for passing the time.

After picking for a while, they ended up buying all the magazines together.

While the four girls were choosing books, two boys curiously came over to look, but they just stood there for a moment before turning to leave.

Chen Guiliang quickly called out, "Hey, handsome, don't go. These books of mine are very yellow and very violent!"

As soon as he said this, not only did the two boys stop, but Tao Xue and the others also looked at him in surprise.

One of the boys asked curiously, "Which one is very yellow?"

Chen Guiliang pointed to the great works of contemporary masters. "These are all very yellow, full of dirty jokes from beginning to end. Look at this one, *Big Breasts & Wide Hips*. You tell me, isn't that title yellow?" He then pointed to Yu Hua's *To Live*. "That book is very violent. Everyone dies except the main character."

Tao Xue let out a chuckle, understanding now that Chen Guiliang was just pulling their legs.

Chen Guiliang continued to spin his tales, successfully luring the two boys to squat down and browse the books.

For Chen Guiliang, it didn't matter if they bought anything or not. Just having them there to draw a crowd was enough.

When you're running a stall, as long as you have a crowd, more and more people will gather out of curiosity. The worst thing is for it to be deserted, with passersby not even bothering to glance over.

Chen Guiliang didn't let even the four girls who had bought magazines leave. He told them he and Guo Xiaosi were best buddies, making up celebrity anecdotes about Guo Xiaosi, which left Tao Xue completely spellbound.

A few more people came over one after another, gathering around the stall to listen to Chen Guiliang's bullshitting.

In the blink of an eye, the bell for the end of class rang.

The flow of people here suddenly surged. Seeing the circle formed under the big tree, students passing by ran over to see what was going on.

"Goodbye, Senior. We're heading back to class," Tao Xue waved happily. She planned to find this Senior Zhang Wei in Class 1 of the third year to discuss literature whenever she had time.

Chen Guiliang was also very happy. Counting his money, he called out, "Take care, Junior!"

After another round of nonsense, the bell for the start of class rang, and the ten-minute break was over. Chen Guiliang had already sold over twenty of his old books, and all his old magazines were sold out.

Because they were indeed very cheap.

Moreover, this shoddy school had produced a Guo Xiaosi, so the literary atmosphere was particularly strong at the moment, and there were many students who enjoyed leisure reading.

Chen Guiliang stretched contentedly. Students are so easy to fool!

"Damn it, my suitcase!"

A guy with a center-parted hairstyle and glasses stood in front of Chen Guiliang's bookstall, swearing.

The worn-out suitcase, temporarily used to hold books, was obviously his.

Chen Guiliang's eyes lit up. "Yo, County Magistrate Xie, long time no see."

The guy with glasses was taken aback. "What County Magistrate Xie?"

Chen Guiliang raised his hand, bent his fingers, and said mystically, "This old master has divined by his fingers that you will become a county magistrate at the age of 40."

The guy with glasses, filled with pride, lifted his head high, his nostrils facing the sky. "A county magistrate is nothing. I'm not going to be an official. I'm going into business in the future, making games like Chen Tianqiao and Ding Lei. When my company goes public, I'll be the richest man in China!"

Chen Guiliang grumbled inwardly: You'll make games my ass. I'm the one who's going to be a damn game developer in the future.

Old Wang, I heard you have 90,000 words of stockpiled chapters. Is that true?
